newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish premier names new industry minister.
newsitem.headline: Danish premier names new industry minister.

text.p: Danish Premier Poul Nyrup Rasmussen on Monday moved Transport Minister Jan Troejborg to the trade and industry ministry in a shuffle following the Centre Democrat party's resignation from the ruling coalition.
Troejborg is a member of Rasmussen's Social Democrats.

The key portfolios of Finance, Economy, Foreign Affairs and Defence were unchanged, a government statement showed, although the economy ministry would take over regulation of financial sectors previously under the eye of the finance ministry.
Economy Minister Marianne Jelved previously oversaw only the mortgage industry.

As part of the shakeup Rasmussen increased the cabinet strength of his Radical Liberal coalition partners to four from three, with the appointment of college principal Ebbe Lundgaard as culture minister, and reduced the overall size of the government to 19 ministers from 20.
Other changes included the reassignment of Justice Minister Bjoern Westh to traffic, Research Minister Frank Jensen to justice and Culture Minister Jytte Hilden to research, the statement said.
Analysts did not expect the changes to alter government policies or have any great effect on financial markets.

Centre Democrat leader and Trade and Industry Minister Mimi Jakobsen said on December 20 that she and Health Minister Yvonne Herloev Andersen were leaving the centre-left coalition but that the party's five members of parliament would continue to vote with the minority government.
She said that her party, which had presented itself to voters as a bulwark in government against the left, was uneasy about growing dependence on parliament's far left.

The government made deals with leftists holding pivotal parliamentary seats to win their support for its 1997 budget after the breakdown of its talks with the Conservatives. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33 969650
